correctness.rationale: The proof counts, for every fixed complete matching M and every position k of the dissenting agent, exactly one priority permutation if and only if her suffix favorite is M(e). Summing over k gives integer t_x, with sum t_x=n and (n-1)! matchings per x giving normalization. The support/Pareto equivalence uses exchange with a common-order agent for a non-record x and the sum of assigned common-object indices to rule out improvement for a record x. As k advances, suffix winners are monotone, run lengths are exactly the index gaps of right-to-left records, and every composition is constructed by ranking its cumulative endpoints first. Independent random insertion of a uniform preference permutation yields independent right-to-left record indicators with probabilities 1/j, hence Stirling-generating polynomial, expectation and variance. Independently rebuilt RSD on ALL exceptional orders and ALL agent priority orders for n=2,3,4,5: 2,3,5,7 distinct sorted t-shapes respectively, and every matching multiplicity matched the closed t_x rule (not generalized from the test). Finite tests support but do not replace all-n proof.

value.rationale: The joint deterministic-matching lottery, unlike the individual marginal assignment matrix, gives exact ex-post support, concentration and multiplicity spectra in a natural one-dissenter perturbation of unanimity. The all-n composition classification and exact record-count distribution connect a mechanism-level outcome statistic to permutation records and answer a motivated allocation question; this is more than renaming the standard record lemma.

final_claim: For all n>=2 and any strict dissenter preference with n-1 common-order agents, the full labeled random-priority matching lottery has exact masses t_(M(e))/n!, supported precisely on Pareto-efficient matchings. As the dissenter order varies, positive masses realize every ordered composition of n, with p(n) sorted shapes; under an independent uniformly sampled dissenter order the number R of distinct suffix-winning objects has the unsigned Stirling-first-kind distribution, while the number of supported complete matchings is (n-1)!R, with exact profile frequencies and support expectation/variance.
limitations: Square balanced allocation, strict complete preference rankings, exactly one dissenter, uniform random priority; impartial-culture assumption only for rank-frequency statement.
